qualification: Pre-fix Lut::from_3dl accepted non-finite (`NaN`/`inf`) node and mesh values because `f32::NAN.clamp(0.0, 1.0)` returns `NaN`; Lut::from_cube and Lut::from_spi1d accepted non-finite or inverted/degenerate input domains (`DOMAIN_MIN >= DOMAIN_MAX`, `LUT_1D/3D_INPUT_RANGE`, `From`); Lut::is_identity for Lut::One probed only 17 grey steps instead of checking every 1D table entry against its domain, causing Grade::is_identity and Grade::apply to skip 1D LUTs with changes between the 17 probe points; and MasteringDisplay::from_corners / from_payload accepted zero or collinear chromaticity coordinates (`y == 0.0`, `x + y > 1.0`, or collinear R/G/B corners such as an all-zero 24-byte placeholder MDCV payload) and `max_luminance == 0.0` or `min_luminance > max_luminance`, poisoning Primaries::rgb_to_xyz and Grade::new with NaN.

Updating src/color/lut.rs and src/color/hdr.rs requires finite `.3dl` node/mesh values, enforces finite `min < max` input domains in `.cube` and `.spi1d`, checks every entry of all three channels in `Lut::is_identity` for `Lut::One`, and validates positive CIE `y`, `x + y <= 1.0`, non-collinear primaries (`rgb_to_xyz`/`xyz_to_rgb` finite), and `0.0 <= min_luminance <= max_luminance` (`max_luminance > 0.0`) in `MasteringDisplay::from_corners`.

Synthetic fixtures in tests/fixtures/playback-errors/color/ verify `.3dl` NaN rejection, `.cube` and `.spi1d` inverted/NaN domain rejection, 1D LUT full-entry identity checking in `Grade::apply`, and placeholder/collinear MDCV rejection with clean HDR10 Grade fallback.
4 focused integration tests, 69 root color unit tests, 68 fvid-codecs color unit tests, and 5 offline Python fixture unit tests pass.

Adobe/Resolve `.cube`, Autodesk `.3dl`, Sony Pictures Imageworks `.spi1d`, and SMPTE ST 2086 / CIE 1931 chromaticity domain invariants govern these checks. All fixtures are pure synthetic offline files requiring neither FFmpeg nor network access.
